text: 5. [3:465] Employment Discrimination Claims: Whether CGL policies provide coverage for employment discrimination is subject to a similar analysis as claims for wrongful termination and sexual harassment: a. [3:466] No “bodily injury” coverage: Employment discrimination claims generally are not covered under standard-form CGL “bodily injury” coverage for the following reasons: (1) [3:467] Often no “bodily injury”: Employment discrimination claims typically seek damages for emotional distress, mental anguish, etc. Most courts hold emotional distress does not constitute “bodily injury” under a CGL policy (¶ 3:356). [See Aim Ins. Co. v. Culcasi (1991) 229 CA3d 209, 220, 280 CR 766, 772] (2) [3:468] No accidental “occurrence”: CGL policies cover only accidental “occurrences” (see ¶ 3:357); and acts of employment discrimination are generally intentional, not accidental—even when no discriminatory effect was intended. [Loyola Marymount Univ. v. Hartford Acc. & Indem. Co. (1990) 219 CA3d 1217, 1225, 271 CR 528, 532] b. [3:469] “Personal injury liability” coverage?
